key_insight: The paper proposes Structure-Driven Inversion (SDI), which solves inverse problems by exploiting intrinsic mathematical or physical structure instead of relying only on iterative objective minimization.
engineering_relevance: SDI could improve inversion efficiency, interpretability, and multi-parameter decoupling in computational science and engineering workflows such as imaging and PDE-based inverse problems.
method: MSDI: builds a pseudo-inverse in the spectral domain using unitary diagonalization.
PSDI: uses physical structure via virtual-source projection for waveform inversion imaging.
PSDBP: applies three structural projections to deep neural networks through a physical-system analogy.
evidence_signal: The abstract is conceptual and taxonomy-focused; it does not report experiments, benchmarks, or quantitative results.
watch_item: The framework is new and currently supported by representative methods, so practical robustness and scalability across diverse inverse problems still need validation.
paper_title: Structure-Driven Inversion: A New Paradigm for Solving Inverse Problems
